items.claim: Test 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' no longer exercises the no-stack branch
items.consequence: The original plain object `{ message: 'original' }` had no `stack`, so the test hit the `else if (Error.captureStackTrace)` branch in GraphQLError.js. A real Error always has a stack, so the test now takes the `originalError.stack` branch and duplicates 'uses the stack of an original error'. The fallback path loses its only coverage while the test name still claims to cover it.
items.proposed_fix: Keep a Flow-valid original error with no stack, e.g. `const original = new Error('original'); delete original.stack;` (or set stack to undefined via a cast to any), so the captureStackTrace / Error().stack fallback in GraphQLError.js is exercised again.

residual_risks: Flow itself was not run (execution allowance covers mocha only); the claim that the changed tests type-check under @flow strict, and that `// $FlowFixMe` on the inspect('"') line suppresses a real error rather than being an unused suppression, is unverified.

The GraphQLError.js change widens the declared constructor `nodes` type to include null; the runtime code already tolerates null (tests pass null), so risk is limited to Flow typing of downstream callers.
testing_gaps: Fallback stack-capture branch in GraphQLError (originalError without a stack) is no longer covered by any test in the changed file.
